title: Payments — outbox, consumer, API
description: The four questions an operator asks during an incident, in the order they ask them: is anything piling up, is anything moving, is anything being thrown away, and is the front door still answering.

panels.title: Outbox backlog — records waiting to be published
panels.description: The first number to look at when Kafka is unwell. It grows while nothing can be published, which is the outbox doing its job, and falls once the relay drains. A flat non-zero line means the relay is not running at all.

panels.title: Outbox sweeps per second, by outcome
panels.description: A failing sweep is still a sweep: if this drops to nothing rather than turning red, the relay is gone, not blocked.

panels.title: Events handled per second — counted against duplicate
panels.description: Duplicates are at-least-once delivery working. A burst of them after a restart is healthy; a steady stream of them is a relay republishing something it cannot mark.

panels.title: Consumer group lag
panels.description: Read from the cluster, not from the consumer: a consumer that has stopped cannot report its own lag, and that is the moment the number matters.

panels.title: Dead letters per second, by reason
panels.description: Anything here is a record no retry will fix. Undecodable means bytes nobody can read; refused means the consumer understood it and will not take it.

panels.title: API requests per second, by status
panels.description: The question this answers during a broker outage: is the front door still taking payments while the events pile up behind it.

panels.title: Under-replicated partitions
panels.description: Non-zero means a broker is missing from an ISR somewhere. With min.insync.replicas=2 the writes keep going until the second replica goes too.
